{{recipe}}
== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* 1 stick (½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]], softened
* 2 medium [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplants]], [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] ½ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] thick
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* Freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
* [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|Olive oil]]

== Procedure ==
#[[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] garlic into butter. Shape into a narrow log using [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]] or wax paper, and refrigerate until needed.
#Sprinkle all sides of eggplant with salt. Let sit 15 minutes or until it "sweats". Leave it without touching.
#Rinse eggplant. Pat dry with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]], and [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] with olive oil.
#Season liberally on both sides with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Grill|grill]] to medium-high heat.
#Add eggplant to grill, and cook until marked and slightly charred on both sides.
#Place a pat of butter mixture on top of each piece and wait until butter is melted before serving.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Save the extra garlic butter. Use it instead of regular butter for things like chicken, fish, and steak.
* Making the eggplant "sweat" helps bitter flavors come out of the eggplant.
